resources.string: Grab the screen from anywhere, crop it, and share it — without saving anything to your device.

Choose Circle to Share as the digital assistant app (Default digital assistant app → Circle to Share). This makes the assistant gesture — press and hold the power button, or swipe up from a bottom corner — open the crop overlay. If a \"Use screenshot\" toggle is shown there, enable it.

If your device doesn\'t hand screenshots to third-party assistants, the accessibility service captures the screen instead. Under Accessibility → Circle to Share, turn on the main \"Use\" toggle. (This also powers the Quick Settings tile and the floating button below.)
Invoke your assistant (hold the power button, or swipe up from a bottom corner), circle what you want, then hit Share. Tip: the test button below captures this screen.

Ways to trigger a capture — use any of them:

• Power button: press and hold (works via the assistant role from step 1). Set under System → Gestures → Press & hold power button → Digital assistant, if it opens the power menu instead.

• Corner swipe: swipe up from a bottom corner — another way to invoke the assistant from step 1, if enabled in your system settings.

• Quick Settings tile: tapping it closes the shade and captures what was behind it. To add it, pull down the shade, tap the pencil/edit button, and drag the "Circle to Share" tile into your tiles — or use the button below, if your Android version offers it. Needs the accessibility fallback (step 2) enabled.

• Floating button (below): the app's own always-on-screen bubble you can tap from any app. Drag it anywhere; it stays out of the way. Needs the accessibility fallback (step 2) enabled.
The tile is already in your Quick Settings.
Couldn\'t open the add-tile prompt. Add it from the shade\'s edit screen instead.
Enable the accessibility fallback (step 2) first — the Quick Settings tile runs on it.
Unlock the device first to capture the screen.
A small draggable bubble on screen. Tap it to capture, crop, and share from anywhere.
Enable the accessibility fallback (step 2) first — the bubble runs on it.
Drag to crop — or share the full screen
Circle what you want — or share the full screen
Tap to restore your last crop
Draw a freeform loop around what you want and its outline becomes the crop box. Turn off to drag a rectangle directly.
Crop edges snap to the buttons, cards, and images that were on screen. Element positions are read only at the moment of capture and never stored. Needs the accessibility fallback (step 2).
Enable the accessibility fallback (step 2) first — snapping reads element positions through it.
Highlights QR codes found in the capture — tap one to copy its content or open its link. Scanning happens entirely on this device; nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
Not a color — use a hex code like #FFCA28
Couldn\'t get a screenshot. Enable the fallback in the Circle to Share app, or turn on \"Use screenshot\" in assistant settings.
Set Circle to Share as your assistant app first.
Couldn\'t open settings on this device.

Lets Circle to Share capture the screen when you trigger it — with the assistant gesture, the Quick Settings tile, or the app\'s floating button — so you can crop and share it. Screen content (element positions) is read only at the moment of capture, and only to align the crop box with what\'s on screen. Nothing is captured until you trigger it, nothing is saved to your device, and nothing ever leaves it.
